title: Newborn infant physical examination (NIPE) basics
summary: What the newborn physical examination covers and the key findings to refer on before discharge.
redFlags: Heart murmur, or absent/weak femoral pulses.
Abnormal tone, movements, or level of alertness.

blocks.heading: Timing
bullets: A full NIPE examination is carried out within 72 hours of birth, with a further check by a GP at around 6–8 weeks — VERIFY exact local timing and pathway.

blocks.heading: What's examined
bullets: Eyes — including the red reflex, to screen for cataract and some other eye conditions.
Heart — listening for murmurs and checking femoral pulses.
Hips — screening for developmental dysplasia (e.g. Ortolani/Barlow manoeuvres where trained).

blocks.heading: If a red flag is found
bullets: Refer to the paediatric team per local pathway — do not simply advise 'routine follow-up' for any of the red flags above.
Document clearly what was found and the referral made.

blocks.heading: Screening alongside NIPE
bullets: Newborn hearing screen and the newborn blood spot (bloodspot) screening programme run alongside the physical examination.
VERIFY exact local timing and consent process for each screening programme.
